newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1.00- trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1.00- trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, extending Thursday's losses amid surplus hog supplies and generally lower wholesale pork prices, cash dealers said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to the plant in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range $55.00-$56.00.
Illinois top plant prices could range $52.50-$53.00 and Indiana top prices for hogs delivered to the plant door could range $53.00 to $53.50, the dealers said.
Abundant interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts on Tuesday contributed to Thursday's declines, sources there said.

Interior Iowa hog receipts for Tuesday were confirmed at 107,000 head versus the estimate of 95,000, said USDA. Thursday's estimate was 110,000 head, compared with 94,000 a week ago and 100,000 a year ago.
Weak pork prices lent further pressure, with steep declines in fresh loins and butts overshadowing slight increases in hams and bellies, livestock dealers said.
USDA said fresh loin and butt prices fell $6.00 to $8.00 per cwt Thursday morning while hams were quoted steady to $1.00 higher and bellies, steady to $1.00 higher.
There were 67.0 fabricated pork loads sold and 8.5 loads of trimmings as of midday, according to USDA.
Many packer buyers said they were well supplied with live inventories for Friday and nearly done buying Saturday hogs.
